To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the pheromones cAM373 and cAM373 are encoded by genes that are part of the conjugative transfer operon, (b) the genes encoding cAM373 and its inhibitor are divergently transcribed, (c) the gene encoding the inhibitor is located downstream of the gene encoding cAM373, (d) the cAM373 inhibitor is a 22-amino acid peptide that contains an N-terminal cysteine and is processed from a larger precursor,

(1) the pheromones of E. faecalisis and S. aureus are structurally related, (2) they are synthesized by a common mechanism, (3) the genes encoding them are located in the chromosome and are adjacent to genes encoding the corresponding peptide transporters, (4) they are expressed in the absence of plasmids, and (5) they are subject to the same regulation by the corresponding peptide transport proteins.

the Enterococcus faecalisspecific pheromone-responsive plasmids pCF10 and pAM373 are encoded by a common genetic element that also encodes the sex pheromomes of the Staphylococcusspecific plasmids pSK41 and pGO1.

it has led to the discovery and characterization of a novel family of sex pheromomes that are produced by the human pathogens E. faecium and S. aureus.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the Enterococcus pheromones are a class of peptide molecules that are secreted by plASMID-CONTAINING CELLS, and they act on plasmid-free recipient cells to promote adherence and plasmid acquisition, thus enabling the transfer of antibiotic resistance determinants.

the enterococcal sex pheromome cAM373 and its cognate receptor are highly specific for E. faecium and E. faecallis and are not found in other enterococci, such as E. durans, which has been used in the dairy industry for years without any reported problems.
sex pheromomes are not only produced by Gram-positive bacteria, but are also produced by Gram-negative species.
